title: Queensland
wiki_lead:
Queensland (locally  KWEENZ-land,  commonly abbreviated as QLD or Qld) is a state in northeastern Australia, the second-largest and third-most-populous state in Australia. It is bordered by the Northern Territory, South Australia and New South Wales to the west, south-west and south, respectively. To the east, Queensland is bounded by the Coral Sea and the Pacific Ocean; to the state's north is the Torres Strait, separating the Australian mainland from Papua New Guinea, and the Gulf of Carpentaria to the north-west. With an area of 1,723,030 square kilometres (665,270 sq mi), Queensland is the world's sixth-largest subdivision of any country on earth; it is larger than all but 16 countries. Due to its size, Queensland's geographical features and climates are diverse, and include tropical rainforests, rivers, coral reefs, mountain ranges and white sandy beaches in its tropical and sub-tropical coastal regions, as well as deserts and savanna in the semi-arid and desert climatic regions of its interior.
Queensland has a population of over 5.7 million, concentrated in South East Queensland, where nearly three in four reside. The capital and largest city in the state is Brisbane, Australia's third-largest city and comprising fully half of the state's population. Ten of Australia's thirty largest cities are located in Queensland, the largest outside Brisbane being the Gold Coast, the Sunshine Coast, Townsville, Cairns, Ipswich, and Toowoomba. 24.2% of the state's population were born overseas. The state has the highest inter-state net migration in Australia.
Queensland was first inhabited by Aboriginal Australians, with the Torres Strait Islands inhabited by Torres Strait Islanders. Dutch navigator Willem Janszoon, the first European to land in Australia, explored the west coast of the Cape York Peninsula in 1606. In 1770, James Cook claimed the east coast of Australia for the Kingdom of Great Britain. In 1788, Arthur Phillip founded the colony of New South Wales, which included all of what is now Queensland. Queensland was explored in subsequent decades, and the Moreton Bay Penal Settlement was established at Brisbane in 1824 by John Oxley. During the Australian frontier wars of the 19th century, colonists killed tens of thousands of Aboriginal people in Queensland while consolidating their control over the territory.
On 6 June 1859 (now commemorated as Queensland Day), Queen Victoria signed the letters patent to establish the colony of Queensland, separating it from New South Wales and thereby establishing Queensland as a self-governing Crown colony with responsible government. Queensland was named for Queen Victoria, by the authority of Queen Victoria, based on a suggestion from Queen Victoria. Queensland's colonial economy was largely agricultural, and sugar and cotton sectors relied on blackbirded South Sea Islander labour.
Queensland was among the six colonies which became the founding states of Australia with Federation on 1 January 1901. Since the Bjelke-Petersen era of the late 20th century, Queensland has received a high level of internal migration from the other states and territories of Australia and remains a popular destination for interstate migration.
Queensland has the third-largest economy among Australian states, with strengths in mining, agriculture, transportation, international education, insurance, and banking. Nicknamed the Sunshine State for its tropical and sub-tropical climates, Great Barrier Reef, and numerous beaches, tourism is also important to the state's economy.

grok_lead: Queensland is a state comprising the north-eastern section of the Australian mainland, along with several offshore islands, and is the second-largest subnational entity in Australia by land area at 1,727,000 square kilometres. Its population reached 5,647,468 as of 31 March 2025, representing about 20.5% of Australia 's total and concentrated primarily in the southeastern urban corridor led by the capital city of Brisbane. The state spans diverse geographical features, from tropical rainforests and the world's largest coral reef system to arid interior regions, supporting an economy generating over $510 billion annually through sectors dominated by resource extraction, agriculture, and tourism. Originally settled by Europeans as the Moreton Bay penal colony in 1824 and part of New South Wales, Queensland achieved separation as a self-governing British colony on 10 December 1859 following Queen Victoria's approval of the Letters Patent on 6 June of that year, named in her honour to reflect loyalty to the Crown. Upon Australia's federation in 1901, it joined as one of the six founding states, retaining significant autonomy in areas such as resource management and regional development, which have driven its growth amid debates over environmental impacts from mining and agricultural expansion. Queensland's development has been marked by pioneering inland exploration, such as the Burke and Wills expedition in 1860-61, and labour-intensive industries including sugar production reliant on Pacific Islander workers from the late 19th century, contributing to its identity as a resource-rich frontier state with ongoing tensions between economic imperatives and ecological preservation.
